blocks.text: Branches are checked top to bottom and only the first match runs. Order therefore matters: put the most specific condition first. With temp > 20 checked before temp > 30, a 35-degree day would print 'Warm'.
condition ? a : b is an expression that produces a value, so it can be assigned or returned. Use it for simple value choices; nested ternaries quickly become unreadable.
Handle invalid cases first and return early. This removes nesting and keeps the main logic at the lowest indentation level, which reviewers look for.

items: if (x = 5) assigns instead of comparing and is always truthy. Linters flag it; use ===.
Always use braces. Without them only the next statement belongs to the if, and adding a second line later silently runs unconditionally.
switch compares with ===, so switch ('1') never matches case 1, and a missing break falls through to the next case.
Comparing floating-point results with === inside a condition (if (price === 0.3)) can fail due to rounding.
